summary: AI observability has become essential as LLM applications move into production, where unpredictable model behavior, silent quality regressions, and runaway token spend can severely impact reliability and budgets. Modern tools go beyond traditional APM by tracing LLM calls, evaluating output quality, detecting anomalies, and attributing costs. In 2026 the market is consolidating around platforms that offer predictable scaling, OpenTelemetry-based integration, and the ability to pinpoint why AI systems fail.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end traces, token usage, latency, cost breakdowns, and evaluation metrics for LLM and agent applications, with deep native tracing for LangChain and LangGraph.
features: Detailed cost and token breakdowns per trace
tools.pricing: Seat-based plus usage. Free tier for individuals; paid plans add per-seat fees plus per-trace overage charges. At high volume, trace costs run roughly 5-10% of underlying LLM API spend for trace-heavy workloads.
tools.best_for: Teams whose architecture is powered by LangChain or LangGraph and want zero-config, deeply integrated observability that justifies vendor coupling.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: Request-level cost, token usage, latency, and spend attribution by user or department via a lightweight proxy sitting in front of LLM APIs like OpenAI.
features: One-line base-URL change for instant integration
Cost governance and spend tracking in under five minutes
Request logging, caching, and rate limiting
tools.pricing: Request-based (usage) pricing with a generous free tier; scales with request volume rather than seats, making it predictable for cost-control use cases.
tools.best_for: Teams primarily focused on fast, lightweight cost visibility and governance over OpenAI credit usage without heavy architectural integration.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B Weave)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, evaluations, model performance, and experiment metrics across both ML and LLM workloads for unified monitoring.
features: Weave tracing for LLM app calls and chains
Unified ML experiment tracking and model lifecycle management
Evaluation and comparison of model/prompt versions
Good fit for teams running both ML and LLM workloads
tools.pricing: Free tier for individuals and small projects; usage/seat-based paid plans for teams and enterprise with custom pricing.
tools.best_for: ML-mature teams wanting unified observability across traditional ML models and LLM applications in one platform.

tools.name: Arize AI (Phoenix)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, embeddings, drift, data quality, and evaluation metrics, bringing ML observability practices into LLM tracing and monitoring.
features: Enterprise Arize platform for scaled production monitoring
tools.pricing: Phoenix is open-source and free to self-host; Arize enterprise platform is usage/seat-based with custom pricing. Free tier available.
tools.best_for: ML-oriented teams that want to apply established ML observability habits (drift, embeddings, evals) to LLM systems, with an open-source option.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: Traces, token usage, cost, latency, and evaluation metrics with an open-source, self-hostable trace store supporting multiple frameworks.
features: Multi-framework support (not tied to one SDK)
OpenTelemetry integration into enterprise observability stacks
tools.pricing: Self-hosting is free (pay only for compute and storage); managed cloud offers usage-based pricing with predictable scaling and a free tier.
tools.best_for: Self-hosted teams wanting an open-source, multi-framework observability platform with predictable, usage-based scaling.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM traces, token usage, latency, and spans using OpenTelemetry-standard instrumentation that works across any stack and exports to existing observability backends.
features: Works across any framework and stack
Exports to existing OTel-compatible backends (Datadog, New Relic, etc.)
Avoids vendor lock-in by standardizing telemetry
tools.pricing: Open-source and free to use; costs come from the chosen backend/observability vendor you export data to. Managed Traceloop offering has usage-based pricing.
tools.best_for: Multi-framework setups and teams that want standards-based, vendor-neutral LLM telemetry integrated into existing observability stacks.

cost_tips: Implement prompt caching and response caching to avoid paying for repeated or near-identical requests, which can dramatically cut token spend on common queries.
Right-size your model selection by routing simple tasks to cheaper, smaller models and reserving frontier models for complex reasoning, rather than defaulting every call to the most expensive option.
Use a proxy or observability layer (e.g., Helicone or Langfuse) to track per-user, per-department, and per-feature spend so you can set budgets, alerts, and quotas before costs run away.
Reduce token usage by trimming system prompts, compressing or summarizing context, limiting max output tokens, and batching requests where latency allows.
